subject.title: [Feature]: Add a visible browser panel to the Control UI for login handoff and browser management

question: Should the browser login handoff be a host-owned Control UI browser panel now, wait for generic plugin UI entry points, or be narrowed to backend manual-action/status plumbing first?
rationale: The source already has browser RPC primitives, but exposing same-session browser state in the UI crosses UX, authorization, redaction, and resume-policy boundaries that code inspection cannot choose for maintainers.

options.title: Build host-owned browser handoff panel
options.body: Add a Control UI browser panel backed by existing browser status/profile/tab APIs with explicit manual-login pause, redacted status, target context, and authorized same-state resume.

options.title: Wait for plugin UI entry points
options.body: Use PR #80388 or its successor to provide placement first, then build the browser panel as a browser-owned contribution if maintainers want this outside core navigation.

options.title: Narrow to backend handoff primitives
options.body: Define LOGIN_REQUIRED/manual-action events, doctor/inspect status, and resume semantics before committing to a visible browser-management UI.

recommendation.title: Build host-owned browser handoff panel
recommendation.body: Add a Control UI browser panel backed by existing browser status/profile/tab APIs with explicit manual-login pause, redacted status, target context, and authorized same-state resume.

likelyOwner.reason: The maintainer discussion and recent adjacent Control UI tab work point to steipete as the best available product/security decision owner in the inspected history.
